title: Why America Is Running Out of Munitions
gist: An FP Live event page previewing a discussion with CSIS Missile Defense Project director Tom Karako on how deeply the Iran war has depleted U.S. munitions stockpiles — with high-end Patriot and THAAD interceptor inventories reportedly down as much as 80 percent — and what it would take, likely years, to replace them amid competing needs in Europe and the Indo-Pacific.

themes.theme: Munitions depletion scale and replenishment timeline

insights.claim: By some accounts, U.S. inventories of high-end Patriot and THAAD interceptors may be depleted by as much as 80 percent after the war with Iran this year, with replacement potentially taking years even as military planners worry about simultaneous needs in Europe and the Indo-Pacific.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: An 80% depletion figure for top-tier U.S. missile-defense interceptors is a concrete, alarming data point directly relevant to defense-contractor replenishment demand forecasts (Lockheed Martin/RTX-linked Patriot and THAAD production) and to assessing residual U.S. missile-defense capacity available for Europe or a Taiwan contingency.

insights.claim: CSIS Missile Defense Project director Tom Karako has tracked how deep the U.S. munitions shortfall runs and what it would take to fix it, framing the discussion around the future of American military preparedness given competing demands across multiple theaters.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Flags a named subject-matter expert (Tom Karako, CSIS Missile Defense Project) as a source to follow for ongoing, detailed assessment of U.S. munitions-stockpile recovery — useful for tracking future granular data on the replenishment timeline.
